questions.question: A pole 10 m long rests slantly against a vertical wall AB making an angle 30º with the horizontal (ground). Find how far the foot of the pole is from the wall (in metres).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using basic trigonometry, the distance from the wall (Base) can be calculated directly as:

Base = Hypotenuse × cos(θ)

Base = 10 × cos(30°)

Base = 10 × (√3 / 2) = 5√3 m

**∴ The correct answer is 5√3 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/916a75326d954d06b1f20fb8bf306281f8d160b404431a67054583ba4b13dcfd.png] 

**Given:**

Length of the pole (Hypotenuse AC) = 10 m

Angle made by the pole with the ground (∠ACB) = 30°

**Formula Used:**

In a right-angled triangle, cos(θ) = Base / Hypotenuse

**Calculations:**

Let the vertical wall be AB and the pole be AC.

The distance of the foot of the pole from the wall is represented by BC.

⇒ In ΔABC, cos(30°) = BC / AC

⇒ √3 / 2 = BC / 10

⇒ BC = 10 × (√3 / 2)

⇒ BC = 5√3 m

**∴ The correct answer is 5√3 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios

In a right-angled triangle, sin(θ) = Perpendicular / Hypotenuse, cos(θ) = Base / Hypotenuse, and tan(θ) = Perpendicular / Base.

Common Values

For standard angles: sin(30°) = 1/2, cos(30°) = √3/2, and tan(30°) = 1/√3.

Pythagoras Theorem

In any right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides: Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular².

questions.question: A straight vertical pole was broken during a cyclone in such a way that its top touched the ground at a distance of 6sqrt 3 m from the bottom of the pole and made and angle of 30° with the horizontal. What was the height (in m) of the pole?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a **30°-60°-90°** triangle, the side ratios are **1 : √3 : 2**.

Distance from base (√3 part) = 6√3 m ⇒ 1 unit = 6 m.

Height of broken part (1 unit) = 6 m and Hypotenuse (2 units) = 12 m.

Total height of **vertical pole** = 6 + 12 = 18 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 18 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3eb7e80e74a742c56d4abc107331ea0efe2ecace20019979a21be259dc4f678c.png] 

**Given:** Distance BC = 6√3 m, Angle of elevation θ = 30°.

**Formula Used:** tan θ = Perpendicular/Base; cos θ = Base/Hypotenuse.

⇒ In triangle ABC, tan 30° = AB / BC

⇒ 1/√3 = AB / 6√3

⇒ AB = 6 m (Height of standing part)

⇒ cos 30° = BC / AC

⇒ √3/2 = 6√3 / AC

⇒ AC = 12 m (Length of broken part)

⇒ Total height of pole = AB + AC = 6 + 12 = 18 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 18 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios

Common values: tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, tan 60° = √3.

Height and Distance

The total height of a **broken object** is the sum of the vertical segment and the slant hypotenuse segment.

Standard Triangle Proportions

For a 30° angle, the ratio of Height : Base : Hypotenuse is always 1 : √3 : 2.</p

questions.question: A vertical pole of 28 m height casts a 19.2 m long shadow. At the same time, find the length of the shadow cast by another pole of 52.5 m height.
questions.solution:
Given:

The height of the pole is 28 m and it casts a shadow 19.2 m long.

The shadow cast by the tower is 52.5 m long.

Concepts used:

The similarity of triangles using AA(angle-angle) rule

The ratio of corresponding sides of similar triangles is equal.

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9111169371a287175cf6c6005ef29e6a65eea4fa6b9884aab5ea8048fb795486.png] 

In ΔABC and ΔEDC,

∠ABC = ∠EDC (each 90°)

∠ACB = ∠ECD (Common angle)

∴ ΔABC ∼ ΔEDC (By AA rule).

⇒ AB/ED = BC/DC

⇒ 52.5/28 = BC/19.2

⇒ BC = 52.5 × 19.2/28

⇒ BC = 36 m.

**∴ The length of the shadow cast by another pole of 52.5 m height**** **is 36 m.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ab777b338e076ebcb2cdb89e2ff2843a1499dfb3df00b235186d1c5e1857e625.png] __Confusion Points__

As the position of the sun is fixed at a particular time and both buildings are on the same sides of the sun, the angle made by the shadow with the horizon must be equal.

questions.question: A and B are two points on the same side of a ground, 50 meters apart. The angles of elevation of these points to the top of a tree are 60° and 30°, respectively. What is 40% of the height of the tree (in m)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For angles of elevation **30°** and **60°** on the **same side** of a tower/tree, the **height** (H) is related to the **distance** (d) between the points by the formula: **H = (d × √3) ÷ 2**.

⇒ **Height of the tree** = (50 × √3) ÷ 2 = 25√3 m.

⇒ Required value = 40% of 25√3 = 0.4 × 25√3 = 10√3 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 10√3 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Distance between points A and B = 50 m. Angles of elevation are 60° and 30°.

**Formula:** tan θ = Perpendicular ÷ Base

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8c1cd6fef18ba3b752b5a416a72297f537b9112c73d490e5222d3b62fdffbbab.png] 

Let the **height of the tree** be H and the distance from the base of the tree to point A be x.

⇒ In Δ PAC (smaller triangle): tan 60° = H ÷ x

⇒ √3 = H ÷ x → x = H ÷ √3 --- (i)

⇒ In Δ PBC (larger triangle): tan 30° = H ÷ (x + 50)

⇒ 1 ÷ √3 = H ÷ (x + 50) → x + 50 = H√3 --- (ii)

⇒ Substitute (i) in (ii): (H ÷ √3) + 50 = H√3

⇒ 50 = H√3 − (H ÷ √3)

⇒ 50 = (3H − H) ÷ √3

⇒ 50 = 2H ÷ √3 → H = 25√3 m.

⇒ 40% of height = (40 ÷ 100) × 25√3

⇒ Required value = 0.4 × 25√3 = 10√3 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 10√3 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Distance formula for same side

When points are on the same side of a tower of height H, the distance d = H(cot θ₂ − cot θ₁), where θ₁ > θ₂.

Distance formula for opposite sides

When points are on opposite sides of a tower, the distance d = H(cot θ₁ + cot θ₂).

Standard Trigonometric Ratios

For 30°: tan 30° = 1/√3, cot 30° = √3 | For 60°: tan 60° = √3, cot 60° = 1/√3.</p

questions.question: A ladder leaning against a wall makes an angle θ with the horizontal ground such that cos theta = dfrac{5}{13}. If the height of the top of the ladder from the foot of the wall is 18 m, then what is the distance (in m) of the foot of the ladder from the wall?
questions.solution:
** Given:**

cosθ = 5/13

The height of the top of the ladder from the foot of the wall is 18 m.

**Concept Used:**

Cosθ = Base/ Hypotenuse

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fe9a9c457f87f66c1031b4e72a77fb5a2ab4307aa58bc83401a411c5bb2876fe.png] 

cosθ = 5/13 = Base/ Hypotenuse

Let, Base (BC) = 5x and Hypotenuse (AC) = 13x where x is a constant

Accordingly, AB = 18 m

From ΔABC, 

18² + (5x)² = (13x)²

⇒ 18² = 169x² - 25x²

⇒ 324 = 144x²

⇒ x² = 324/144

⇒ x = 3/2

Base (BC) = 5 × 3/2

⇒ 7.5

**∴ The distance of the foot of the ladder from the wall is 7.5 m.**

questions.question: When the sun’s angle of depression changes from 30° to 60°, the length of the shadow of a tower decreases by 70 m. What is the height of the tower?
questions.solution:
**Given****∶**

Decrease in the length of shadow of the tower = 70 m

Initial angle of depression = α = 30°

Final angle of depression = β = 60°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9d481cff62e2c63ca6e82398a6481c27fffd45197d3b15017482047d3ace612b.png] 

**Calculation****∶**

Let the height of the tower be AC.

Initial angle of elevation = 30°

Final angle of elevation = 60°

In ΔDAC,

tan60° = AC/AD

⇒ √3 = AC/AD

⇒ AD = AC/√3 ----(1)

In ΔBAC,

AB = AD + 70

tan30° = AC/AB

⇒ 1/√3 = AC/(AD + 70)

⇒ AC = 1/√3 × (AD + 70)

Put the value of AD from (1),

⇒ AC = 1/√3 × (AC/√3 + 70) = AC/3 + 70/√3

⇒ AC × 2/3 = 70/√3

⇒ AC = (70 × 3) / (2 × √3) = 35√3 = 35 × 1.73 = 60.55 m

questions.question: As observed from the top of a lighthouse, 42 m high above sea-level, the angle of depression of a ship sailing directly towards it changes from 30° to 45°. The distance travelled by the ship during the period of observation is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If the angle of elevation (or depression) of a tower of height h changes from θ₁ to θ₂ as an object moves directly towards it, the distance travelled is:

Distance = h × (cot θ₁ − cot θ₂)

Here, h = 42 m, θ₁ = 30°, θ₂ = 45°

Distance = 42 × (cot 30° − cot 45°)

Distance = 42 × (√3 − 1)

**∴ The correct answer is 42(√3 − 1) m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6e7eb57492f4e8ed7e1520931e65b2310f3a7ad59fb5b406a3d3d4ea60fbae88.png] 

**Given:**

Height of the lighthouse (AB) = 42 m

Angle of depression at initial position C = 30° ⇒ Angle of elevation ∠ACB = 30°

Angle of depression at final position D = 45° ⇒ Angle of elevation ∠ADB = 45°

**Formula Used:**

In a right-angled triangle, tan θ = Perpendicular ÷ Base

**Calculations:**

In right-angled triangle ΔABD,

⇒ tan 45° = AB ÷ BD

⇒ 1 = 42 ÷ BD

⇒ BD = 42 m

In right-angled triangle ΔABC,

⇒ tan 30° = AB ÷ BC

⇒ 1 ÷ √3 = 42 ÷ BC

⇒ BC = 42√3 m

The distance travelled by the ship is CD, which is the difference between BC and BD.

⇒ Distance CD = BC − BD

⇒ Distance CD = 42√3 − 42

⇒ Distance CD = 42(√3 − 1) m

**∴ The correct answer is 42(√3 − 1) m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Heights and Distances (Trigonometry)

The angle of elevation is the angle formed between the horizontal reference line and the line of sight when looking up at an object. The angle of depression is the angle formed when looking down from a height.

Two Objects on the Same Side

If two objects are observed on the ground from a tower of height h at angles θ₁ and θ₂, the distance separating them is easily calculated as h(cot θ₁ − cot θ₂).

Two Objects on Opposite Sides

When two objects are situated on opposite sides of a central tower of height h, having respective angles of elevation θ₁ and θ₂, the total distance between them is h(cot θ₁ + cot θ₂).
</p

questions.question: The angle of elevation of the top of a tall building from the points M and N at the distances of 72 m and 128 m, respectilvely, from the base of the building and in the same straight line with it, are complementary. The height of the building (in m) is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__
When **angles of elevation** from two points at distances **a** and **b** from the base are **complementary**, the **height (h)** of the building is the **geometric mean** of the distances.

Formula: h = √(a × b)

h = √(72 × 128) = √(9 × 8 × 8 × 16)

h = 3 × 8 × 4 = 96 m

**∴ The correct answer is 96 m.**

**__Alternate Method__**
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/466eb545ad866fadd931dad9fb865211cd9a6d19672d214dc70a94ecb69d9991.png] 
**Given:** Distance **a = 72 m**, Distance **b = 128 m**. Angles are **θ** and **(90−θ)**.

**Formula Used:** tan(θ) = Opposite / Adjacent

⇒ In first triangle: tan(θ) = h / 72

⇒ In second triangle: tan(90−θ) = h / 128

⇒ cot(θ) = h / 128 [Since tan(90−θ) = cot(θ)]

⇒ tan(θ) × cot(θ) = (h / 72) × (h / 128)

⇒ 1 = h² / (72 × 128)

⇒ h² = 9216

⇒ h = √9216 = 96 m

**∴ The correct answer is 96 m.**

**__Additional Information__**

Complementary Angles Rule

If angles of elevation from two points on the same side of a tower are complementary, the height is h = √(ab).

Trigonometric Identities

tan(90° − θ) = cot θ and tan θ × cot θ = 1 are key identities for solving such height and distance problems.

Geometric Mean

The result h = √ab shows that the height is the geometric mean of the two horizontal distances from the base.</p

questions.question: A 20 m long ladder rests against a wall so that the angle between the ladder and the wall is 30°. How far (in m) is the base of the ladder from the wall?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

In a **30°−60°−90° right-angled triangle**, the side opposite the **30° angle** is always **half of the hypotenuse**.

The **ladder** acts as the **hypotenuse** (20 m) and the distance from the wall is the side **opposite to the 30° angle**.

Required Distance = 20 m ÷ 2 = 10 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 m.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the **ladder** (Hypotenuse) = 20 m

**Angle** between ladder and wall = 30°

**Formula Used:**

In a right-angled triangle, sin θ = Opposite Side ÷ Hypotenuse

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/83956c24a67c793652171e6873079c2bc996571ff26adcc3e88ca7d310491247.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the distance of the **base of the ladder** from the wall be **x**.

⇒ In right-angled triangle ABC, sin(30°) = BC ÷ AC

⇒ 1 ÷ 2 = x ÷ 20

⇒ x = 20 × (1 ÷ 2)

⇒ x = 10 m

**∴ The correct answer is 10 m.**

**__Additional Information__**

30°−60°−90° Triangle Rule

The sides of a 30°−60°−90° triangle follow the ratio 1 : √3 : 2. The side opposite 30° is x, the side opposite 60° is x√3, and the hypotenuse is 2x.

Trigonometric Ratios

Key values to remember: sin 30° = 1/2, cos 30° = √3/2, tan 30° = 1/√3. Use **SOH CAH TOA** as a mnemonic for ratios.

Complementary Angles

If the angle with the wall is 30°, the angle with the ground is 90° − 30° = 60°. Therefore, base distance = Ladder × cos(60°) = 10 m.</p

questions.question: A ladder 10 m long rests against a vertical wall making an angle of 30° with the wall. How high up (in m) does it reach the wall from the ground? (Take sqrt 3 = 1.73.)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When a **ladder** makes an angle θ with a **vertical wall**, the height reached (h) is the **adjacent side** of the triangle.

Formula: **Height** = **Ladder Length** × cos(θ)

Height = 10 × cos(30°) = 10 × (√3 ÷ 2)

Height = 5 × 1.73 = 8.65 m

**∴ The correct answer is 8.65 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: **Ladder length** = 10 m, **Angle with wall** = 30°, √3 = 1.73.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bcdb500b623781a331f22921d12c91c9dc6c2429256733cd6ae668c27cb9cff5.png] 

In the right-angled triangle **ABC**, let **AC** be the wall, **BC** be the ground, and **AB** be the ladder.

⇒ **Hypotenuse** (AB) = 10 m

⇒ **Angle** with wall (∠BAC) = 30°

⇒ cos(∠BAC) = Adjacent side (AC) ÷ Hypotenuse (AB)

⇒ cos(30°) = Height (h) ÷ 10

⇒ (√3 ÷ 2) = h ÷ 10

⇒ h = (10 × √3) ÷ 2

⇒ h = 5 × 1.73

⇒ h = 8.65 m

**∴ The correct answer is 8.65 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios

For a right-angled triangle, sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse and cos θ = adjacent/hypotenuse.

Angle with Ground vs Wall

If the angle with the wall is θ, the angle with the ground is (90° − θ). For θ = 30°, the angle with the ground is 60°.

Pythagoras Theorem

In any right triangle, (Base)² + (Height)² = (Hypotenuse)².

Common Trig Values

cos(30°) = √3/2 ≈ 0.866; sin(30°) = 1/2 = 0.5; tan(30°) = 1/√3 ≈ 0.577.</p

questions.question: From the top of a house A in a street, the angles of elevation and depression of the top and foot of another house B on the opposite side of the street are 60° and 45°, respectively. If the height of house A is 36m, then what is the height of house B?(Your answer should be nearest to an integer.)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b86d43966eecf6cf2b88a9fc1c7e4e91e9ed8522b9ee2511ad1b6c87895510e6.png] 

Given, AP = 36m

In△PAB

⇒ tan45 = PA/AB

⇒ 1 = 36/AB

⇒ AB = 36

⇒ AB = PR = 36

In △PQR,

⇒ tan60 = QR/PR

⇒ √3 = QR/36

⇒ QR = 36√3 = 36 × 1.7 = 61.2

⇒ QB = QR + RB [RB = PA]

⇒ QB = 61.2 + 36 = 97.2

⇒ QB ≈ 98

questions.question: Suhas, a 3.15 m tall tree, and a building are positioned such that their feet on the ground are collinear and the tree is located between Suhas and the building. The tree is located at a distance of 7.5 m from Suhas and at a distance of 45 m from the building. Further, the eyes of Suhas, the top of the tree, and the top of the building fall in one line, and the eyes of Suhas are at a height of 1.8 m from the ground. Find the height (in m) of the building.
questions.solution:
**Concept used**

Height and distance; Similarity of triangles

**Calculation**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a813d98a932683efc170b0f56d21a606718815fd65be5d116b6e12e572cc1d38.png] 

According to the above diagram,

h/(45 + 7.5 +x) = 3.15/(7.5 + x) = 1.8/x,

Where,

h = height of the building,

x = distance to the point along the ground from the tree aline with the tips of the building, the tree and the eye level of the observer

Hence, 3.15/(7.5 + x) = 1.8/x 

⇒ 3.15x - 1.8x = 1.8 × 75

⇒ 1.35x = 1.8 × 75

⇒ x = 10

h/(45 + 7.5 +x) = 1.8/x

⇒ h = 0.18 × 62.5

h = 11.25 m

**Hence, the height of the building = 11.25 m**

questions.question: A pole 23 m long reaches a window which is 3sqrt5 m above the ground on one side of a street. Keeping its foot at the same point, the pole is turned to the other side of the street to reach a window 4sqrt15 m high. What is the width (in m) of the street?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The length of the pole = 23 m

The first window is 3√5 m above the ground and the second window is 4√15 m above the ground.

**Formula used:**

In a right-angled triangle,

Base = √(Hypotenuse² - Perpendicular²)

**Calculation:**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/653b57e007cd822dc84f2c0bb4aab03f4f06c436f134f5ebee857b4f0c8b170b.png] **

Here, the width of the street = BC

In ΔABO,

BO = √(AO² - AB²)

= √(232 - 3√52)

= √(529 - 45)

= √484

= 22 m

In ΔOCD,

CO = √(DO2 - DC2)

= √(232 - 4√152)

= √(529 - 240)

= √289 = 17 m

Then, BC = BO + CO 

= 22 + 17 

= 39 m

**∴ The width (in m) of the street is 39 m**

questions.question: A mirror is placed on the ground facing upwards. A man sees the top of a tower in the mirror which is at a distance of 105 m from the mirror. The man is 0.5 m away from the mirror, and his height is 1.5 m. Find the height of the tower (in metres).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Height to Distance is constant for both objects due to the law of reflection.

Height of Man / Distance of Man = Height of Tower / Distance of Tower

1.5 / 0.5 = Height / 105

3 = Height / 105

Height = 105 × 3 = 315 m

**∴ The correct answer is 315 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

Height of man (AB) = 1.5 m

Distance of man from mirror (BM) = 0.5 m

Distance of tower from mirror (MD) = 105 m</p

questions.question: Suhas, a tree, and an 11.25 m tall building are positioned such that their feet on the ground are collinear and the tree is located between Suhas and the building. The tree is located at a distance of 7.5 m from Suhas and at a distance of 45 m from the building. Further, the eyes of Suhas, the top of the tree, and the top of the building fall in one line, and the eyes of Suhas are at a height of 1.8 m from the ground. Find the height (in m) of the tree.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Height of the building = 11.25 m

Distance of the tree from Suhas = 7.5 m

Distance of the tree from the building = 45 m

Height of Suhas's eyes from the ground = 1.8 m

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/261f6b2a6c9b213090e8cc9a06495d14cbc855b81479c1b21dcf22c4759636b7.png] 

Distance of Suhas from the building = 7.5 m + 45 m = 52.5 m

The length of BC = 11.25 - 1.80 = 9.45

Now In the triangle, ABC,

⇒ tan θ = 9.45/52.5.....(1)

Now In the triangle, AGH.

⇒ tan θ = x/7.5.....(2)

From 1 and 2

⇒ x/7.5 = 9.45/52.5.

⇒ x = 1.35 m

⇒ Height of the tree = 1.35 m + 1.8 m

⇒ Height of the tree = 3.15 m

**∴ The height of the tree is 3.15 m.**
